answer: Meteg: present (a separate vertical stroke is printed below the vowel row). Host: most likely ע with its chataf patach, but uncertain. The stroke sits toward the left edge of the ע area, close to the boundary with ד, so ד cannot be ruled out with certainty. It is not under ב.
visible_evidence: The whole word בעדנו and its lower points are visible. Under ב is a patach dash, with a second short dash just below it. Under ע is the chataf patach (a dash plus two vertical dots). Under ד the vowel dots read as tsere. Under נ the dots are hard to make out. Below the vowel row, at roughly x≈155 and y≈210–235, there is a clear vertical stroke that stands on its own. It is longer than a vowel stem and lower than the sheva or chataf dots, and no ink from a neighboring line touches it. That fits a meteg. Its horizontal position is near the left side of ע / the right side of ד, so I can't pin its host down confidently. The second short dash under ב is unexplained. It could be part of the vowel or stray ink, and it is not a meteg.
